You're investigating a git branch in the repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover (a design-to-code handover repo for client Zimmermann, component tag prefix `zimm-`). Working directory is already checked out on branch `feature/browser-preview-and-full-kit-catalog`; `main` also exists locally, up to date with origin. READ-ONLY investigation: do not edit files, do not switch branches, do not commit.

Background: this branch restructures the design token CSS and consolidates duplicated focus-ring styles, plus makes a couple of Figma-verified corrections to the button component. Two commits describe this — verify the actual code against these claims:

COMMIT 2f0f59a: "Split token CSS by category..." — splits common.css's flat :root token block into 02-design/library/tokens/{colors,typography,spacing}.css by category. common.css becomes a thin @import aggregator plus still-provisional Motion tokens and shared/reset styles. Claims common.css's public path and behavior are unchanged (nothing that already links it needed updating), and claims 121 custom properties before and after the split, verified matching. Also describes the button.js conversion being cross-checked against the real Figma component (node 901:2897): fixed an :active state bug that ignored variant/inverse, filled in four previously-unspecified inverse combinations with confirmed values, fixed a missing explicit CSS class for the "large" size.

COMMIT 6ece7d6: "CSS dedup pass..." — moves zimm-button.css to 02-design/library/tokens/buttons.css (imported by common.css), reasoning that button classes are reused directly by other components' native markup, not just zimm-button's own renderer, so every page gets them for free. zimm-button.js (the render function) stays in its own element folder. Introduces a `--zimm-focus-ring` composite token in tokens/colors.css, consolidating 9 byte-identical focus-visible outline declarations across 8 components onto it: add-to-wishlist, banner, card-baseline, card-editorial, cat-links-aside, page-toolbar, toolbar-category, and button's own three focus states. Also corrects a trailing comment in common.css that still described the pre-migration Shadow DOM architecture.

YOUR JOB — verify against actual files (current branch HEAD state, plus `git diff main..HEAD` for before/after):

1. Read 02-design/library/common.css as it exists on `main` (`git show main:02-design/library/common.css`) and as it exists now on HEAD. Confirm it changed from a flat :root token block to an @import aggregator, and list exactly what it now imports/contains.
2. Read 02-design/library/tokens/colors.css, typography.css, spacing.css, buttons.css in full. Count the total custom properties (`--zimm-*` or similar, count every `--` declaration) across common.css + all four token files on HEAD, and compare to the total count of custom properties in common.css on `main` alone. Confirm whether the "121 before and after, matching" claim actually holds — show your counting method and the numbers, don't just assert it matches.
3. Confirm `--zimm-focus-ring` is defined in tokens/colors.css, and grep for `focus-visible` across 02-design/library/elements/ to confirm it's now referenced (not hand-duplicated) in add-to-wishlist, banner, card-baseline, card-editorial, cat-links-aside, page-toolbar, toolbar-category, and button. Report which of these 8 actually use the token vs. which (if any) still hand-roll their own outline declaration — a real discrepancy would be valuable to flag.
4. Confirm zimm-button.css now lives at 02-design/library/tokens/buttons.css (check `git diff main..HEAD -- 02-design/library/elements/button/` for the deletion and `tokens/buttons.css` for the addition), and confirm common.css actually @imports it.
5. Diff zimm-button.js and zimm-button.css between main and HEAD. Confirm: (a) the :active state now properly accounts for variant/inverse combinations (show the relevant CSS rules/selectors), (b) there's now an explicit CSS class for the "large" size that wasn't there on main.
6. Confirm the trailing comment in common.css was actually updated (quote the old vs new comment text).

Report back with one line per claim: CONFIRMED / PARTIALLY CONFIRMED / DISCREPANCY, with concrete evidence (counts, file:line, quoted snippets). End with anything surprising or inconsistent you noticed that isn't mentioned above. Keep it under 500 words, lead with verdicts.
